Formulation  
A 19-year-old university student with no significant psychiatric history presents with new onset dysuria, increased urinary frequency, and lower abdominal ache, likely indicating a urinary tract infection (UTI). Predisposing factors include IBS and allergy to Clindamycin. Recent first-time cannabis use unlikely related to symptoms but noted as a lifestyle factor. Social support is adequate. Symptoms cause some anxiety impacting daily activities (university attendance). No current mental health diagnosis or risk factors identified. Protective factors include good insight and appropriate help-seeking behavior.

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Anxiety related to symptoms consistent with suspected urinary tract infection  
- Patient Goal(s):  
  • Achieve resolution of urinary symptoms  
  • Reduce anxiety related to symptoms and health concerns  
- Clinical Goal(s):  
  • Confirm diagnosis with urine analysis  
  • Initiate effective treatment for UTI  
  • Monitor and manage anxiety symptoms  
- Actions (Patient):  
  • Provide urine sample at designated clinic for testing  
  • Start prescribed antibiotic course (Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin 3-day course, dose/route/frequency not documented)  
  • Maintain adequate hydration and take paracetamol for pain as needed  
  • Monitor symptoms for development of fever, back pain, vomiting, or worsening condition  
  • Avoid cannabis use in future as advised  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  • Arrange urine sample collection and laboratory testing  
  • Prescribe appropriate antibiotic treatment for UTI  
  • Provide education on symptom monitoring and when to seek urgent care  
  • Counsel patient regarding substance use risks  
  • Arrange follow-up within one week if symptoms persist or worsen  

Secondary Problem: Not recorded  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes  
- Topics Covered: UTI symptoms, treatment adherence, hydration, pain management, symptom monitoring for complications, advice on substance use  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Fever, back pain, vomiting, persistent or worsening urinary symptoms  
- Coping Strategies: Drinking plenty of fluids, using paracetamol for discomfort, seeking medical review if symptoms deteriorate
